assets.name: React + TypeScript + MapLibre GL JS Frontend
assets.description: Browser-based SPA for map visualization, feature inspection, and dataset management. Optional deck.gl for advanced visualization.
assets.technology: React (TypeScript strict mode), MapLibre GL JS, ESLint + Prettier

assets.name: GraphQL API Server (Strawberry / FastAPI)
assets.description: Primary backend. ASGI framework hosting code-first GraphQL (Strawberry), multipart file uploads, Pydantic v2 validation. All data operations go through here.
assets.technology: Python 3.12+, FastAPI 0.115+, Strawberry 0.250+, Pydantic v2, Uvicorn

assets.name: Martin Vector Tile Server
assets.description: Standalone Rust tile server from MapLibre team. Reads directly from PostGIS. Serves binary MVT tiles via REST: GET /{layer}/{z}/{x}/{y}.

assets.name: PgBouncer Connection Pooler
assets.description: Multiplexes application connections to PostgreSQL. Required for 10K concurrent user scale.

assets.name: PostGIS Spatial Database
assets.description: Primary spatial data store. Tables: dataset (metadata), feature (normalized polygons + properties as JSON), ingestion_run (processing records). SQLAlchemy 2.x + GeoAlchemy2 ORM. Alembic migrations.
sensitiveData: feature properties (may contain PII or proprietary data)

assets.name: Redis Cache and Celery Broker
assets.description: Dual role: (1) cache for expensive spatial query results, (2) message broker and result backend for Celery. No authentication documented.

assets.name: Celery Background Workers
assets.description: Persistent background jobs: ingestion, spatial processing, exports. Uses Redis broker. Monitoring via Flower. DuckDB for batch processing within workers.

assets.name: DuckDB Spatial Processor
assets.description: In-process batch spatial data processing within Celery workers. Larger-than-memory streaming. Native GeoParquet read/write. Batch only — never serving.

assets.name: Object Storage
assets.description: Stores raw uploaded files with provenance. S3-compatible or local filesystem. Files kept outside web root.

assets.name: CDN / Edge Cache
assets.description: Edge caching for vector tile requests. Absorbs repeat tile requests from concurrent users.

assets.name: GDAL/OGR (via Fiona)
assets.description: Native C/C++ library for GIS format I/O. 200+ format support. Content-based format detection.

assets.name: Shapely / GEOS
assets.description: Geometry operations wrapping GEOS C++. Union, intersection, buffer, simplify, validate. Vectorized ufuncs. Releases GIL during C ops.

assets.name: pyproj / PROJ
assets.description: CRS detection, transformation, reprojection. Wraps native PROJ C library.

threats.title: No authentication architecture — all endpoints accessible anonymously
threats.description: No authentication mechanism is specified in any document. All GraphQL mutations (upload, delete) and queries (dataset listing, feature data) are accessible to anonymous network clients. The Martin tile server serves tiles without authentication. This is the single largest security gap identified.
recommendedMitigations: Design authentication architecture before implementation begins — add to ARCHITECTURE.md
Implement OAuth2/OIDC with a proven identity provider
Require authentication on all mutations and sensitive queries
Proxy tile requests through authenticated API, or implement signed tile URLs

threats.title: No authorization model — all users have equal access to all data
threats.description: No RBAC, ABAC, or ownership model is defined. The data model has no owner/user field. No admin role exists. Once authentication is added, all authenticated users will have identical access to all datasets and operations.
recommendedMitigations: Add owner_id/created_by to dataset model
Implement dataset-level ownership: only owner can update/delete
Define RBAC with at least user and admin roles
Enforce authorization in GraphQL resolvers

threats.title: Native C/C++ library exploitation via crafted GIS input
threats.description: GDAL/OGR, GEOS, and PROJ are C/C++ libraries with historical CVEs for buffer overflows and memory corruption. Crafted GIS files could achieve code execution within Celery workers, which have database access. Multiple upstream sources confirm this threat and the planned subprocess isolation control.
recommendedMitigations: Implement subprocess isolation with resource limits (memory, CPU time, filesystem)
Apply seccomp/AppArmor profiles to GIS parsing subprocesses
Run GIS processing in dedicated containers with no network access
Monitor GDAL, GEOS, PROJ CVE feeds and update promptly
threats.residualRisk: Medium — new CVEs are discovered periodically

threats.title: Shapefile ZIP archive path traversal
threats.description: Crafted ZIP archives with path traversal entries (../../) could write files outside the extraction directory. Both INITIAL-PLAN.md and CODING-CONVENTIONS.md acknowledge this risk.
recommendedMitigations: Validate all ZIP entry paths — reject '..' and absolute paths
Extract to isolated temp directory and validate before moving
Verify Shapefile-specific extensions only
Enforce maximum extraction size

threats.title: Redis without authentication enables cache poisoning and task injection
threats.description: Redis has no AUTH documented. Any network-accessible process can poison cached queries, inject Celery tasks, modify job state, or flush the cache. Combined with Celery pickle deserialization (CT-12), this enables remote code execution.
recommendedMitigations: Enable Redis AUTH with strong password
Use Redis ACLs for role separation
Bind to internal interfaces only
Enable TLS for Redis connections in production

threats.title: GraphQL query depth/complexity abuse causes API and database DoS
threats.description: Without enforced depth/complexity limits, deeply nested or cartesian-product GraphQL queries can exhaust API memory, CPU, and PostGIS connections. Documented as a convention but not implemented.
recommendedMitigations: Implement Strawberry depth validation (max 10)
Implement cost-based complexity analysis
Set per-query timeout (30s)
Consider persisted queries in production

threats.title: Unlimited file upload size enables resource exhaustion
threats.description: No specific upload size limits are defined. ASGI-layer limits are mentioned as a convention. Multi-GB uploads exhaust disk, memory, and processing time.
recommendedMitigations: Configure specific maximum upload size (e.g., 500MB)
Implement streaming upload processing
Set per-user upload quotas
Monitor storage utilization

threats.title: Expensive spatial operations on large polygons cause database DoS
threats.description: Spatial operations on 50K+ vertex polygons are CPU-intensive. ARCHITECTURE.md explicitly identifies this risk. Crafted queries or datasets could lock PostGIS for extended periods.

existingControls.control: Celery workers with timeouts for large ops

recommendedMitigations: Set PostgreSQL statement_timeout for API queries
Route expensive operations to Celery with hard time limits
Implement geometry complexity limits for interactive queries
Use PostGIS cost estimation to reject overly expensive queries
threats.residualRisk: Medium — legitimate large dataset queries are inherently expensive

threats.title: No rate limiting on any endpoint
threats.description: No rate limiting documented. Unlimited requests enable resource exhaustion, brute-force attacks (once auth exists), and API abuse.
recommendedMitigations: Implement API-level rate limiting (per-IP and per-user)
Apply stricter limits to upload and processing endpoints
Use CDN-level rate limiting for tiles

threats.title: No TLS for inter-service communication
threats.description: No TLS documented for internal connections. SQL queries, spatial data, cache contents, and task messages traverse the network in plaintext.
recommendedMitigations: Enable TLS for PostgreSQL and Redis connections
Use encrypted overlay networks in production
Consider mTLS for service-to-service auth

threats.title: Martin serves all PostGIS data without access controls
threats.description: Martin has direct, unrestricted PostGIS read access. No layer filtering, no row-level security, no authentication on tile endpoint. All spatial data is accessible via tile requests.
recommendedMitigations: Configure Martin for specific layers only
Use read-only PostgreSQL user for Martin
Implement PostGIS row-level security for multi-tenant
Proxy tiles through authenticated API or use signed URLs

threats.title: Celery pickle deserialization enables remote code execution
threats.description: Celery defaults to pickle serialization. Combined with unauthenticated Redis (CT-05), an attacker who gains Redis access can inject pickle payloads for arbitrary code execution on workers.
recommendedMitigations: Set CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER = 'json' and CELERY_ACCEPT_CONTENT = ['json']
Enable Celery message signing
Secure Redis with AUTH (CT-05)

threats.title: Zip bomb in Shapefile archive exhausts disk and memory
threats.description: High compression ratio ZIP archives expand to massive sizes on extraction, filling disk and crashing processes.
recommendedMitigations: Check compression ratio before extraction (reject >100:1)
Set maximum total extraction size
Limit ZIP entry count (Shapefiles have 4-7 files)
Extract in quota-limited temp directory

threats.title: Stored XSS via malicious GeoJSON feature properties
threats.trustBoundary: C-ZONE-DATA -> C-ZONE-INTERNET (data stored from upload, rendered in browser)
threats.description: GeoJSON properties stored verbatim in PostGIS and rendered in frontend feature inspector. Malicious HTML/JS in properties executes in other users' browsers.
recommendedMitigations: Sanitize feature properties at ingestion time
Never use dangerouslySetInnerHTML for properties
Implement CSP
Encode when rendering in DOM attributes

threats.title: No audit logging — security events unattributable
threats.description: No audit logging architecture. Dataset operations, authentication events (once auth exists), and admin actions cannot be attributed or investigated.
recommendedMitigations: Implement security audit logging for auth events, CRUD operations, admin actions
Include user identity, action, resource, IP, outcome in audit records
Store in append-only storage
Define retention period

threats.title: No CORS or CSP configuration
threats.description: No CORS or CSP headers documented. Any website can make cross-origin requests to the API. No CSP to mitigate XSS impact.
recommendedMitigations: Configure strict CORS for frontend origin only
Implement CSP headers
Add security headers: X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, HSTS

threats.title: GraphQL introspection exposes full schema
threats.description: GraphQL introspection enabled by default in Strawberry. Provides complete API reconnaissance to attackers.
recommendedMitigations: Disable introspection in production
Or restrict to authenticated admin users

threats.title: No encryption at rest for data stores
threats.description: No encryption at rest for any data store. All data on disk in plaintext.
recommendedMitigations: Enable TDE or encrypted volumes for PostgreSQL
Enable S3 server-side encryption
Document encryption requirements

threats.title: Database credentials at risk of exposure
threats.description: Connection strings with credentials may appear in env vars, Docker Compose files, logs, or Celery metadata.

existingControls.control: No secrets in code, safe logging

recommendedMitigations: Use secrets manager for production
Configure SQLAlchemy to redact connection strings in logs
Audit all log output for credential leaks

threats.title: PgBouncer connection pool exhaustion
threats.description: Long-running spatial queries can hold PgBouncer connections, exhausting the pool for all services.
recommendedMitigations: Configure per-pool limits per service
Set server_idle_timeout and query_wait_timeout
Implement PostgreSQL statement_timeout

threats.title: Celery workers run with full database privileges
threats.description: Workers likely use same DB credentials as API. Compromised worker has full database access.
recommendedMitigations: Create separate PostgreSQL user for workers with minimal grants
Restrict to INSERT/UPDATE on specific tables only

threats.title: DuckDB native parser risks on untrusted GeoParquet
threats.description: DuckDB processes untrusted GeoParquet with native Arrow/Parquet parsers in-process. Crafted files could trigger parser vulnerabilities.
recommendedMitigations: Validate GeoParquet structure before DuckDB processing
Run in resource-limited subprocesses
Keep DuckDB updated

threats.title: Tile request flooding bypasses CDN cache
threats.description: Unique z/x/y tile requests bypass CDN cache, hitting Martin and PostGIS directly.
recommendedMitigations: Rate limit tile requests at CDN/Martin level
Restrict zoom ranges per layer
Pre-generate common tiles

threats.title: Feature properties may expose sensitive source data
threats.description: GIS datasets contain attribute data (owner names, parcel IDs, yield data). Stored and served without filtering.
recommendedMitigations: Allow marking properties as sensitive
Filter properties in API responses based on authorization
Strip sensitive properties from tile attributes

threats.title: No dependency vulnerability scanning
threats.description: No automated dependency scanning configured despite CODING-CONVENTIONS.md requirement.
recommendedMitigations: Enable Dependabot
Add pip-audit and npm audit to CI

threats.title: No data retention or deletion policies
threats.description: Datasets and raw files accumulate indefinitely. No cleanup or lifecycle management.
recommendedMitigations: Define retention policies
Implement cascading dataset deletion

controlsInventory.name: No shell execution with user input
